_note: 第三種集型的事實庫:**同一個宣稱、跨多個領域**。跟 famous(一篇對一篇)和 lineup(一個效應家族的多次重測)都不同 —— 這裡的數字不是效果量,是『這個因素解釋了多少變異』,分領域列出。2026-08-30 建立,每個數字都附 quote(它出自摘要的哪一句)。
_why_new_kind: 10,000 小時法則在 effect_scan 裡分數 24,311,是 22 個候選裡的第一名,而且是第二名的 2.3 倍。但它的頭條數字是**變異數百分比**,套不進 make_episode.thresholds() 的 d / r 兩軌。硬轉成 r=sqrt(R^2) 雖然數學上精確,螢幕上卻會出現一個觀眾去查論文查不到的數字(論文寫 26%,我印 0.51)。所以寧可多一種集型,不要多一個對不上的數字。
_missing_note: 缺的欄位一律留 null 並在 missing 裡點名,**不推估**。統合分析涵蓋幾篇研究、總共多少人,摘要裡沒有,四個來源(OpenAlex / Semantic Scholar / PubMed / Europe PMC)抓到的摘要都一樣。要用就得我自己讀原文,在那之前旁白不准提。

episodes.claim: how much you practise is what separates the best from everyone else

original.title: The role of deliberate practice in the acquisition of expert performance
original.cited_by_approx_note: 文案用的『超過 N 次』。無條件捨去到百位,所以一定是保守的下界。

test.title: Deliberate practice and performance in music, games, sports, education, and professions: a meta-analysis
test.missing_note: 涵蓋研究數與總人數不在摘要裡,四個來源都沒有。**旁白與畫面都不准提**,直到我讀過原文。
test.unit: percent of variance in performance explained by deliberate practice

domains.name: professions
domains.pct_note: 原文是『less than 1%』。存成 1 並標記為上界 —— 畫面與旁白都要唸『less than one percent』,不能唸成 1%。

test.quote: We found that deliberate practice explained 26% of the variance in performance for games, 21% for music, 18% for sports, 4% for education, and less than 1% for professions. [Macnamara, Hambrick & Oswald 2014, abstract]
test.verdict_quote: We conclude that deliberate practice is important, but not as important as has been argued. [same abstract]

episodes.hook: How much you practise is what separates the best from everyone else?
episodes.hook_short: Practice is what separates the best?
episodes.tone_manual_why: 作者自己的結論是『important, but not as important as has been argued』—— 那是『真的有、但比宣稱的小』,不是『不存在』。判 gone 會是**過度宣稱**,而且直接跟我引用的那句話矛盾。這個欄位必須手填:famous_tone 靠信賴區間分檔,這裡沒有信賴區間,讓它自己猜就是拿缺漏當斷言(bystander_effect 那次的錯法)。

episodes.claim: standing in a powerful pose for two minutes makes you more powerful

original.title: Power Posing: Brief Nonverbal Displays Affect Neuroendocrine Levels and Risk Tolerance
original.quote: That a person can, by assuming two simple 1-min poses, embody power and instantly become more powerful has real-world, actionable implications. [Carney, Cuddy & Yap 2010, abstract]
original.n_quote: Carney et al. found that power posing affected levels of hormones such as testosterone and cortisol, financial risk taking, and self-reported feelings of power in a sample of 42 participants [Ranehill et al. 2015, p.653]

test.kind: conceptual replication, experimenter blind to condition
test.title: Assessing the Robustness of Power Posing: No Effect on Hormones and Risk Tolerance in a Large Sample of Men and Women
test.power_quote: Our statistical power to detect an effect of the magnitude reported by Carney et al. was more than 95% [Ranehill et al. 2015, p.653]
test.extra_quote: Neither of the other two behavioral tasks yielded significant differences by condition. [Ranehill et al. 2015, p.654]
test.verdict_quote: Using a much larger sample size but similar procedures as Carney et al. did, we failed to confirm an effect of power posing on testosterone, cortisol, and financial risk taking. We did find that power posing affected self-reported feelings of power; however, this did not yield behavioral effects. [Ranehill et al. 2015, p.654]
test.missing_note: 這一集沒有缺漏欄位 —— 全文讀過,每個數字都附原句。
test._claim_note: 四項都是同一個宣稱的不同量法,所以「4 個裡回來 1 個」是對的說法。
test.say_verdict: The authors put it plainly: using a much larger sample, they failed to confirm an effect on testosterone, cortisol, or financial risk taking. Power posing changed how people said they felt. It did not change what they did.

episodes.hook: Standing in a powerful pose for two minutes makes you more powerful?
episodes.hook_short: Two minutes in a power pose?
episodes.tone_manual_why: 四個結果裡有一個顯著(felt power, p=.017)、三個不顯著。判 gone 是**過度宣稱** —— 有一個真的重現了,而且是原作者也量的那一個。判 held 也不對 —— 那個頻道賣點的三個生理與行為結果全都沒重現。這一集的重點就是**哪一個活下來**,所以定調必須是 shrunk_real 並在片裡講清楚是哪一個。

episodes.claim: you learn better when you are taught in your own learning style

original.title: Learning Styles: Concepts and Evidence
original.journal: Psychological Science in the Public Interest
original.claim_quote: They called this interaction the meshing hypothesis which states that an individual learns better when taught in a mode of instruction (for example listening versus reading) that aligns with their preferred learning style (auditory, visual, respectively). [Rogowsky et al. 2020, Introduction, describing Pashler et al. 2009]
original.note: 這不是一篇提出主張的原始研究,而是**指出這個主張沒有證據、並且訂出該怎麼測**的評論。所以片裡不能說「2009 年有人發現…」——它從頭到尾都在說沒有。
original.say_origin: This one does not come from a study that found it. In 2009 four researchers reviewed the whole literature and reported that almost nobody had run the experiment that could test it. So they wrote down exactly what that experiment would have to look like.

test.kind: experiment following the prescribed design, whole 5th grade
test.title: Providing Instruction Based on Students' Learning Style Preferences Does Not Improve Learning
test.n_quote: Eligible participants included the entire population of 5th graders (ages 10-11 years) enrolled in a public middle school in rural Pennsylvania (N = 136). The actual participants were those students present for three consecutive days during which the study occurred (n = 125; 64 females/61 males).

outcomes.name: taught in their style
outcomes.note: 這就是整個理論要成立的那一項
outcomes.quote: There was not a significant main effect of instruction (F(1, 32) = 1.15, p = 0.29), nor an instruction by learning styles interaction (F(1, 38) = 1.16; p = 0.29).

outcomes.name: listening beat reading
outcomes.quote: A significant main effect for instruction was found (F(1, 110) = 4.92; p = 0.03) with students performing better when listening (M = 36.0, SE = 0.9) than reading (M = 34.4, SE = 0.8). This corresponds to an effect size of eta 2 = 0.04, which is considered small.

outcomes.name: visual types, both tasks
outcomes.quote: There was a significant main effect of learning styles (auditory vs. visual; F (1, 32) = 12.92; p = 0.001) with an effect size of eta 2 = 0.29 ... These results indicate that visual learners were significantly better at both listening and reading comprehension, as compared to auditory learners.
outcomes.name_long: visual types scored higher at both

test.verdict_quote: Results failed to find a significant relationship between auditory or visual learning style preference and comprehension. Fifth graders with a visual learning style scored higher than those with an auditory learning style on listening and reading comprehension measures. As such, and counter to current educational beliefs and practices, teachers may actually be doing a disservice to students by using resources to determine their learning style and then tailoring the curriculum to match that learning style. [abstract]
test.missing_note: 全文(Europe PMC fullTextXML)自己讀過,每個數字都附原句。
test.say_test: In 2020 a team ran it, on the entire fifth grade of one American public school. 125 children. Every child was tested for listening and for reading, and then taught in one mode or the other.
test.say_punch: The thing the whole idea rests on - being taught in your own style - came back at p of zero point two nine. Nothing. But two other things did come back, and neither of them is the theory. Everybody did better listening than reading. And the children labelled visual scored higher at both - reading and listening. That effect was seven times the size of the one that was significant in the other direction.
test.say_verdict: So the label does not tell you how to teach someone. At most it tells you who tests better overall. The authors put it plainly: teachers may actually be doing a disservice to students by using resources to determine their learning style and then tailoring the curriculum to match it.
test._name_note: name 是**畫面上的顯示標籤**(我寫的),不是引文 —— 所以可以為了版面縮短。真正不能動的是 quote 與 stat。原本較長的說法留在 name_long。
test._claim_note: 只有第一項是**那個宣稱本身**(教學方式 × 學習風格的交互作用)。另外兩項是順帶量到的、而且都跟理論無關。所以標題不能寫「3 個裡回來 2 個」——那讀起來像理論部分成立,而真相是**要成立的那一個沒回來**。

episodes.hook: You learn better when you are taught in your own learning style?
episodes.hook_short: Taught in your own learning style?
episodes.tone_manual_why: 要測的那一項(教學方式 × 學習風格的交互作用)p = 0.29,不顯著 → gone。但**片裡必須講清楚有兩件事是顯著的**,而且它們都跟理論無關:所有人聽比讀好(p = 0.03, eta2 = 0.04),以及被歸類成視覺型的人**兩種都比較強**(p = 0.001, eta2 = 0.29 —— 比那個小效應大七倍)。只講「沒效」會漏掉這一集真正的發現:分類沒有告訴你怎麼教一個人,它只告訴你誰考得比較好。

episodes.claim: being paid more to say something you do not believe makes you change your mind less

original.title: Cognitive consequences of forced compliance
original.journal: The Journal of Abnormal and Social Psychology
original.n_note: 71 人受試,11 人資料被剔除,分析用 60 人(每組 20)。**用 60 不用 71** —— 71 是招募數,結論是從 60 來的。
original.quote: The prediction [from 3 and 4 above] is that the larger the reward given to the subject, the smaller will be the subsequent opinion change. [Festinger & Carlsmith 1959]
original.quote_n: Seventy-one male students in the introductory psychology course at Stanford University were used in the experiment.
original.quote_excl: The data from 11 of the 71 Ss in the experiment had to be discarded
original.quote_result: In this condition, the average rating was +1.35 ... significantly different from the Control condition at the .02 level (t = 2.48). ... The average rating in this condition is only -.05 ... The difference between the One Dollar and Twenty Dollar conditions is significant at the .03 level (t = 2.22).

means.scale: -5 to +5, how enjoyable the tasks were

original.say_origin: In 1959 two researchers at Stanford paid people to tell a stranger that a boring task had been fun. Some were paid one dollar. Some were paid twenty. The ones paid one dollar came to like the task more. The prediction was that the bigger the reward, the smaller the change of mind. Sixty people.

test.title: A Multilab Replication of the Induced-Compliance Paradigm of Cognitive Dissonance
test.journal: Advances in Methods and Practices in Psychological Science 7(1)
test.n_note: 4,898 人招募,初步排除後 **3,996** 人進分析。片裡講 3,996,招募數只在說明欄出現。
test.⚠️_scope: **Vaidis 2024 重測的不是 $1 vs $20。** 它重測的是 Croyle & Cooper 1983 實驗一,操弄的是「選擇自由」而不是「報酬多寡」。Vaidis 自己寫:早期研究操弄報酬(引 F&C 1959),後來研究者從操弄報酬改成操弄選擇。所以片裡**必須明講**這一點 —— 講成「$1/$20 被推翻」是假的。誠實的框架是:這個典範有兩半,被大規模重測的那一半塌了。

outcomes.name: choice changed the attitude
outcomes.quote: we did not find a significant difference in postessay attitude between the HC-CE condition (M = 2.60, SD = 1.91) and the LC-CE condition (M = 2.66, SD = 1.99), t(2,751.46) = -0.79, p = .79, d = -0.03, 95% CI = [-0.10, 0.04].

outcomes.name: writing it at all changed it
outcomes.quote: we did find a significant difference comparing the postessay attitude between the HC-CE condition and the HC-NE condition, t(2,408.92) = 6.51, p < .001, d = 0.26, 95% CI = [0.18, 0.34].

test.verdict_quote: Overall, the results call into question whether the induced-compliance paradigm provides robust evidence for cognitive dissonance. [Vaidis et al. 2024]
test.verdict_quote_2: Despite a large sample and an improved methodology, we did not observe the expected effect of choice on attitude. We did observe that performing counterattitudinal behavior, regardless of perceived choice, affected attitudes.
test.say_test: In 2024, thirty-nine laboratories in nineteen countries ran the modern version of the same paradigm. Three thousand nine hundred and ninety-six people. One thing you should know: they did not retest the money. Since the sixties researchers stopped varying the reward and started varying how free the person felt to say no. That is the half they retested.
test.say_punch: The thing the theory needs - feeling you chose it - came back at minus zero point zero three. Nothing. It was measured a second way, and that came back at nothing too. But writing the thing at all, whether or not you felt you had a choice, did move people. Zero point two six.
test.say_verdict: The authors put it plainly: freedom of choice, they write, typically considered a vital component of this paradigm, does not reliably produce attitude change. But note what that does and does not say. It is about this way of testing the idea, on this half of it - the money version has not been retested at this scale. And the debate is live: a commentary responding to this replication was published in the same journal later that year. It is linked below.
test.missing_note: agent 讀過全文,每個數字都附原句。

extra_outcome.name: the same, second measure
extra_outcome.quote: we did not observe a significant difference between the HC-CE condition (M = 1.00, SD = 1.81) and LC-CE condition (M = 0.97, SD = 1.80), t(1,969.56) = 0.38, p = .35, d = 0.017, 95% CI = [-0.071, 0.11].

test._precision_note: 第二個測量 d = 0.017,畫面用兩位小數會印成 0.02 —— 跟論文對不上。而它跟第一項是同一個檢定的第二個測量,畫面上是冗的。移到說明欄用原句完整呈現(extra_outcome)。**通則:畫面只放能用兩位小數如實表示的數字**,其餘留給說明欄。
test.verdict_quote_3: Freedom of choice, typically considered to be a vital component of the induced-compliance paradigm, does not reliably produce attitude change. Consequently, this raises serious doubts about previous findings that stem from this paradigm and certain interpretations of CDT... Consistent with the core principles of CDT, writing a counterattitudinal essay did lead to attitude change.
test.quote_sample: In a total of 39 labs from 19 countries and 14 languages, participants (N = 4,898) were assigned to one of three conditions: writing a counterattitudinal essay under high choice, writing a counterattitudinal essay under low choice, or writing a neutral essay under high choice.
test.quote_paradigm_lineage: In the first studies using this paradigm, participants were asked to perform a counterattitudinal task in exchange for either a small or sizable reward (e.g., Brehm & Cohen, 1962; Festinger & Carlsmith, 1959)... In later studies, researchers shifted from manipulating reward size to manipulating the choice given to participants as a justification for their counterattitudinal behavior (see Linder et al., 1967). [Vaidis et al. 2024 —— 這是「他們沒有重測報酬」的出處]

rebuttal.title: Dissonance in the Induced-Compliance Paradigm: A Commentary on Vaidis et al. (2024)
rebuttal.journal: Advances in Methods and Practices in Psychological Science
rebuttal.⚠️: **我沒有讀過它的內文。** 所以片裡與說明欄只講「有一篇評論回應了這篇重測」並附 DOI,不宣稱它主張什麼。只講重測不提反駁是選擇性呈現;宣稱它說了什麼而我沒讀過,是更糟的那種錯。

test._ocr_note: ⚠️ Festinger & Carlsmith 1959 那份 PDF 的 OCR 把句點讀成逗號:「t = 2,48」實際是 2.48、「t = 2,22」是 2.22、「Ss」被讀成「5s」。agent 抓到的。從 OCR 抄數字前要看它有沒有這種系統性錯讀。

episodes.hook: Being paid more to say something you do not believe makes you change your mind less?
episodes.hook_short: Paid more, change your mind less?
episodes.tone_manual_why: 要測的那一項(選擇自由 → 態度改變)d = -0.03、p = .79 → gone。但片裡**必須**同時講清楚兩件事:(1) 有一項是顯著的(寫了那篇文章本身 d = 0.26),(2) **被重測的不是 $1/$20 那一半**。少講第二點就是把一個範圍有限的結果講成推翻了整個經典實驗。

episodes.claim: telling people a test measures their ability makes the stereotyped group score worse

original.title: Stereotype Threat and the Intellectual Test Performance of African Americans
original.journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 69(5), 797-811
original.n_note: ⚠️ **論文沒有給全篇總樣本數。** 114 是**研究一**的分析人數(招募 117、3 人沒提供 SAT 成績被排除)。片裡只能說「研究一 114 人」,不能說「這篇研究 114 人」。⚠️⚠️ 網路搜尋告訴 agent 是 **76 人 —— 那是錯的**,論文原文寫 117/114。搜尋摘要給的數字不能直接用。
original.quote: Reflecting the pressure of this vulnerability, Blacks underperformed in relation to Whites in the ability-diagnostic condition but not in the nondiagnostic condition (with Scholastic Aptitude Tests controlled). [Steele & Aronson 1995, abstract]
original.quote_n: We recruited 117 male and female. Black and White Stanford undergraduates... The data from 3 participants were excluded from the analysis because they failed to provide their verbal SAT scores. This left a total of 114 participants
original.quote_stat: The ANCOVA on the number of items participants got correct, using their self-reported SAT scores as the covariate (Black mean = 592, White mean = 632) revealed a significant condition main effect, F(2, 107) = 4.74, p < .02
original.say_origin: In 1995 two researchers at Stanford gave Black and White students the same hard verbal test. Half were told it measured intellectual ability. Half were told it did not. The Black students who were told it measured ability scored lower. The students who were told it did not, did not. Study one: a hundred and fourteen people.

test.title: Does stereotype threat influence performance of girls in stereotyped domains? A meta-analysis
test.n_quote: The total sample, obtained by simply adding all participants of the included studies, consisted of N = 3760 girls, of which nST = 1926 girls were assigned to the experimental condition and nC = 1834 girls were assigned to the control condition.

outcomes.name: as published
outcomes.quote: To estimate the overall effect size, we used a random effects model... we found a small average standardized mean difference, g = -0.22, z = -3.63, p < .001, CI95 = -0.34; -0.10, indicating that girls who have been exposed to a stereotype threat on average score lower on the MSSS tests compared to girls who have not been exposed to such a threat.

outcomes.name: with the missing studies added back
outcomes.quote: According to the estimations of the trim and fill method... the funnel plot would be symmetric if 11 effect sizes would have been imputed on the right side of the funnel plot. Actual imputation of those missing effect sizes reduced the estimated effect size to g = -0.07, z = -1.10, p = .27, CI95 = -0.21; 0.06.

test.say_test: In 2015 two researchers pooled every experiment they could find that tested this on schoolgirls in maths, science and spatial tasks. Forty-seven effect sizes. Three thousand seven hundred and sixty girls.
test.say_punch: As published, the effect is there. Minus zero point two two, and it is statistically significant. Then they asked a different question: which studies are missing? The pattern of results implied eleven experiments that were never published. Put those back in, at the size the pattern predicts, and the effect becomes minus zero point zero seven. Not significant. Same literature. Two numbers. The difference is what you assume about the studies nobody wrote up.
test.missing_note: agent 從 Wicherts 自架的論文 PDF 用 pypdf 抽文字讀出,每個數字附原句。
test.verdict_quote: We conclude that publication bias might seriously distort the literature on the effects of stereotype threat among schoolgirls. We propose a large replication study to provide a less biased effect size estimate. [Flore & Wicherts 2015, abstract]
test.say_verdict: The authors' own conclusion is not that the effect is fake. It is that publication bias might seriously distort the literature, and that somebody should run one large replication to get a less biased estimate. That study has not been run. So what you are looking at is not an answer. It is the size of the gap between what got published and what we can actually be sure of.

episodes.hook: Being told a test measures your ability makes you do worse on it?
episodes.hook_short: Told it measures ability, do worse?
episodes.tone_manual_why: ⚠️ 這題政治上敏感,框架必須極度精確。**不能講成「刻板印象威脅是假的」** —— 已發表的估計是 g = -0.22 而且顯著。**也不能只講 -0.22** —— 作者自己做了出版偏誤校正,補回 11 個推估遺失的效果量之後掉到 g = -0.07、p = .27。誠實的故事是:**同一批文獻,兩個數字,差別在於你怎麼假設那些沒被寫出來的研究。**定調 shrunk_real:測得到,但證據強度取決於一個沒人能直接觀察的東西。
episodes._sensitive: 這一集談的是「文獻的證據強度」,不是「某個群體的能力」。旁白全程只講方法與數字,不解釋原因、不外推到任何群體的特質。作者自己呼籲做大型重測 —— 那句要放進去(等 agent 回報原句)。

episodes.claim: showing someone a number first pulls their estimate toward it

original.title: Measures of Anchoring in Estimation Tasks
original.n_note: **MISSING,而且是刻意留白。** 全文在付費牆後,Unpaywall 與 OpenAlex 都確認無 OA 版。網路搜尋給了「N=156(校準組 53 + 錨定組 103)」—— 細節度高到讓人想直接用,但一手驗不到。**不要用。**
original.⚠️_which_paper: ML1 重測的是 **Jacowitz & Kahneman 1995**,不是 Tversky & Kahneman 1974 那篇祖師論文 —— 後者兩邊都沒有直接重測。片裡不能說「他們重現了 1974 年那篇」。
original.say_origin: The idea is older, but the version that got retested is from 1995. You are asked whether something is more or less than a specific number - how many babies are born in the United States each day, how tall is Mount Everest - and then asked to estimate it. The number you were shown first pulls your answer toward it.

test.title: Investigating Variation in Replicability: A 'Many Labs' Replication Project
test.n_quote: This research tested variation in the replicability of 13 classic and contemporary effects across 36 independent samples totaling 6,344 participants.
test.⚠️_no_comparison: **畫面上不放「原始 vs 重測」的對比。** 四題共用同一個原始 d = 0.93,而且 ML1 自己說算不出各題的:原始是 test-retest 設計的點二系列相關,重測是受試者間設計 —— **兩個數字不在同一把尺上**。可以講「四題全數成立」,**不可以講「效果變成 2.6 倍」**。
test.quote_scale: The original anchoring article did not provide sufficient information to calculate effect sizes for individual scenarios, therefore an overall effect size is reported. The Anchoring original effect size is a mean point-biserial correlation computed across 15 different questions in a test-retest design, whereas the present replication adopted a between-subjects design with random assignments. [Klein et al. 2014]
test.say_test: In 2014, thirty-six independent samples ran thirteen classic psychology experiments the same way. Six thousand three hundred and forty-four people. Four of the thirteen were anchoring questions.
test.say_punch: Every one of the four came back. And not narrowly. Across all thirty-six samples, the proportion that found the effect in the right direction and reached significance was one hundred percent. The proportion that went the other way: zero. The proportion that found nothing: zero. One thing I am not going to tell you is how much bigger it got, because the original paper measured it a different way and the two numbers are not on the same scale.
test.say_verdict: So this is one of the ones that held. But be careful with the word. There is a different effect that also gets called anchoring - where a number you were never asked about, just something in the room, is supposed to move your estimate. That one was retested in 2018 on six thousand eight hundred and twenty-six people and came back at zero point zero four. Indistinguishable from zero. Same word. Two different claims. One held, one did not.

episodes.claim: losing something hurts about twice as much as gaining the same thing feels good

original.title: Prospect Theory: An Analysis of Decision under Risk
original.n_note: **沒有總樣本數。** 原文只逐題標 N,值域 64~95。受試者原句:「The demonstrations are based on the responses of students and university faculty to hypothetical choice problems.」—— 假設性選擇、以色列鎊計價。
original.quote: A salient characteristic of attitudes to changes in welfare is that losses loom larger than gains. The aggravation that one experiences in losing a sum of money appears to be greater than the pleasure associated with gaining the same amount. [Kahneman & Tversky 1979]
original.say_origin: The phrase is from a 1979 paper: losses loom larger than gains. Later work put a number on it. The number people quote is about two - losing feels roughly twice as strong as winning the same amount. That number has its own name. Lambda.

test.title: Loss aversion is not robust: A re-meta-analysis

baseline.title: Meta-analysis of Empirical Estimates of Loss Aversion
baseline.quote: We examine 607 empirical estimates of loss aversion from 150 articles... Our analysis indicates that the mean loss aversion coefficient is 1.955 with a 95 percent probability that the true value falls in the interval [1.820, 2.102]. [Brown, Imai, Vieider & Camerer 2024]
baseline.⚠️: ⚠️ 另一篇論文引用這個 CI 時寫成 [1.820, 2.105] —— 以 AEA 一手為準。

outcomes.name: losses smaller, ordered
outcomes.name_long: losses smaller, items ordered by size

outcomes.name: same size, not ordered
outcomes.quote: for studies with symmetric gains and losses and no ordering of items, the loss aversion parameter was approximately 1.07 and not significantly above 1.0, suggesting similar weighting of gains and losses.
outcomes.name_long: same size on average, not ordered by size

test.quote_design: Altering each of these design features reduces the median loss aversion estimate (asymmetric losses by 34%; ordering by 23%), and when both of these features are avoided the median lambda is 1.125 which implies very weak loss aversion. [Yechiam & Zeif 2025]
test.quote_same_data: A meta-analysis of all estimates included in the current analysis yielded an overall lambda of 1.82 (CIlow = 1.73, CIhigh = 1.91) which is approximately the mean observed in Brown et al.'s (2024) original meta-analysis —— 證明不是他們把資料切壞了,而是同一批資料在不同設計下給出不同的數字。
test.say_test: In 2024 a team pooled six hundred and seven estimates of that number from a hundred and fifty papers. The average came out at one point nine five. About two. The classic answer. Then in 2025 another team took the same data and cut it a different way. They asked: does the number depend on how the question was asked?
test.say_punch: It does. When the possible loss was smaller than the possible gain, and the items were ordered by size, the median came out at two point two nine five. When the losses and the gains were the same size on average, and the items were not ordered by size, the median came out at one point one two five. Their model put it at one point zero seven - and that is not significantly above one. One means losing and winning weigh the same.
test.say_verdict: Before you decide they just cut the data badly: they checked. Run the whole pile together and you get one point eight two, which is essentially the number the original meta-analysis reported. The overall result reproduces. It is only when you split it by how the question was built that the number moves. So the argument is not whether people dislike losing. It is how much of that famous number - about two - is the mind, and how much is the questionnaire.
missing: Tversky & Kahneman 1992 的 lambda = 2.25 原文(付費牆,只有二手轉述)
test.doi_note: agent 手上是作者自存的 preprint(沒印 DOI),它從卷期 + article number 推出 DOI 再回 Crossref **驗標題對得上**才給。Crossref 回傳:title 逐字一致、作者 Eldad Yechiam / Dana Zeif、update-to 與 updated-by 皆空(無撤稿或更正)。
test.quote_abstract: The results showed that while the findings of strong loss aversion are replicated when losses are smaller than gains and when gains and losses are presented in an ordered fashion, for studies with symmetric gains and losses and no ordering of items, the loss aversion parameter was approximately 1.07 and not significantly above 1.0, suggesting similar weighting of gains and losses.
test.quote_table: Table 1: Median loss aversion parameter λ in the studies from Brown et al. (2024). Studies are divided according to whether the average absolute size of losses was smaller to that of gains (L<G), equal to that of gains (L=G), or larger (L>G); and whether gains/losses were ordered from the smallest to the largest. k = Number of estimates.
test.⚠️_three_numbers:
**1.07 / 1.08 / 1.125 是三件不同的事,不能混用:**
· 1.125 = 描述統計的**中位數**(Table 1,k = 22)。論文**沒有對它做顯著性檢定** ——
  把「not significantly above 1.0」掛在它上面是錯的。
· 1.07 = **摘要**裡的模型估計,「not significantly above 1.0」是掛在這個上面。
· 1.08 = **內文** meta-regression 的預測值(「a predicted λ estimate of 1.08」)。
旁白說「in their model」而觀眾去 grep 內文模型段,看到的是 1.08 不是 1.07 ——
所以要嘛講清楚是摘要的估計,要嘛兩個都不指定來源只講「their model」並接受這個模糊。
test._label_note: 畫面標籤縮短了,完整說法在 name_long(說明欄用)與旁白裡(「the losses and the gains were the same size on average, and the items were not ordered by size」)。**name 是顯示標籤不是引文,可以為版面縮短;quote 與 stat 不能動。**

episodes.hook: Does losing hurt about twice as much as winning the same amount feels good?
episodes.tone_manual_why: 要成立的那一項(對稱且未排序時 lambda 顯著高於 1)沒有成立 —— 1.07 且與 1.0 無顯著差異。但**不能講成「損失趨避不存在」**:全樣本的 lambda 是 1.82,而且 Brown 2024 那篇 607 個估計的統合分析支持它。誠實的故事是:**那個經典的 2 有多少是實驗設計做出來的。**

_unit_note: 兩種單位:`pct`(變異數百分比,10,000 小時那集)與 `d`(Cohen's d,power posing 那集)。**單位不同,畫面就不同** —— d 沒辦法畫成「佔滿格的幾分之幾」,所以走清單而不是長條。硬用同一種畫法就會出現一個觀眾無法解讀的比例尺。
